newsitem.title: UK: Oftel tells BT to stop "unfair" sales drive.
newsitem.headline: Oftel tells BT to stop "unfair" sales drive.

text.p: Britain's telecoms regulator Oftel said on Monday it had ordered British Telecommunications Plc (BT) to stop an advertising and sales campaign because it was discriminatory and was offering excessively low prices without regulatory permission.
In a statement the regulator Don Cruickshank said, "We have acted firmly because the campaign is not fair competition between operators", adding that BT had breached its licence.

Cruickshank said that the action had followed a period of consultation with BT, prior to the campaign, explaining that, "once the campaign was launched it appeared very different to the one proposed."

He found BT's drive, with a strong emphasis on winning back customers from other operators, had "discriminated unduly in targeting other operators' customers, and had failed to obtain my consent to the below-cost element of the offer".

Initially BT had argued that the deep discounts were mainly intended to help encourage people without phones to sign up with the company, Oftel said, adding that because the offers have now been stopped some such people would be denied the opportunity to benefit.
"But I cannot, even on that account, let pass such licence breaches which the overall effect of the offer represents," Cruickshank concluded.
Last autumn BT had a series of tangles with the regulator over the way company staff talked to customers about the giant company's increasingly active competitors which include cable operators.
